items.description_text: Ctrl+Alt+Solidarity training course is designed for organisations that want to enhance the digital dimension of their work within the ESC programme. Digitalisation influences how young people communicate, participate, learn, engage in communities, and experience volunteering. For organisations active in the European Solidarity Corps, this creates both opportunities and challenges. Digital tools can support inclusion, solidarity, participation, communication, learning, reflection, recognition, and dissemination, but they also raise important questions related to access, ethics, sustainability, quality, and impact. This training course will offer a space for participants to explore the concept of digital youth work, understand its relevance in the ESC context, exchange practices, discover tools and methods, and reflect on how to strengthen digital empowerment in their own organisational reality. The programme will explore how digital youth work and digital empowerment can be meaningfully integrated into European Solidarity Corps projects. Participants will reflect on their organisation’s digital needs, strengths, and gaps, while discovering tools and approaches that can support learning, reflection, recognition, participation, and project quality. Participants will also strengthen their understanding of DigComp, media literacy, critical thinking, and the ethical use of AI, and will be supported in turning these insights into concrete action for their future project cycle and organisational development. The course combines conceptual input, peer learning, practical exchange, self-assessment, reflection, examples of good practice, and action planning. items.description_text: BRIDGE4MOTHERS: Gender-Informed Approaches for Supporting Vulnerable Mothers is an online learning activity designed for professionals working in non-formal learning, youth work, adult education and community-based support. The training introduces participants to the BRIDGE4MOTHERS approach and provides practical, gender-informed and inclusive pedagogical approaches for working with vulnerable mothers. It focuses on creating safe, accessible and supportive learning environments that recognise the different social, educational and personal circumstances that may affect women's participation and learning. Through interactive presentations, discussions, practical activities and shared experiences, participants will explore approaches that can be applied in their own professional and community contexts. The training also introduces relevant learning resources and the BRIDGE4MOTHERS e-learning platform. The activity is particularly relevant for youth workers, trainers, educators, facilitators, VET professionals, adult-learning practitioners and other professionals involved in non-formal learning or community-based support who work with women, mothers or other groups facing barriers to participation. Participants will have the opportunity to: strengthen their understanding of gender-informed and inclusive learning approaches; explore practical methods for engaging vulnerable learners; reflect on barriers to participation and ways to create more inclusive learning environments; exchange experiences and practices with professionals from different European contexts; and access resources and tools that can support their future training and facilitation work. The training is delivered online in English and uses participatory and learner-centred methods. Participants are expected to actively contribute to discussions and activities and to reflect on how the approaches presented can be adapted to their own work. items.description_text: It is dark, our eyes drop heavy, and behind them another world invites us in, no matter if we remember that world upon waking. As our bodies rest, our psyche takes us towards images, memories, emotions and stories that often remain outside our everyday awareness. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is an invitation. An invitation to become curious about the intelligence that lives beneath our usual ways of knowing. Like mycelium moving quietly beneath the forest floor, much of what shapes us remains unseen. An invitation to tend dreams as wild and meaningful parts of ourselves. An invitation to be guided by dreams, movement, art, imagination and nature — allowing them to move with us and within us. And an invitation to explore how these practices can enrich youth work and non-formal education, creating spaces where young people can deepen their relationship with themselves, their communities and the more-than-human world. Dreaming from the Mycelium of the Earth is a 7-day Erasmus+ training course combining dreamwork, embodiment, storytelling, poetry, expressive arts, deep imagination and ecological and nature-based education. The training will offer youth workers and other professionals working with people a space to first experience these approaches themselves and then explore how they can be adapted to their own educational contexts. We believe that meaningful youth work begins not only with methods, but also with the capacity of the practitioner to be present, listen, notice, imagine and create spaces where different ways of knowing and expressing ourselves are welcomed. Throughout the programme, participants will therefore move between personal experience, group learning and professional reflection: What does this practice awaken in me? What does it teach me as a facilitator? How could it support the young people and communities I work with? items.description_text: This international training activity aims to introduce and promote a Self-Assessment Tool for Quality Work with Young People developed in Malta, while strengthening the capacity of youth organisations to embed quality assurance into their everyday practice. Through interactive workshops, peer learning, and practical exercises, participants will develop skills in reflective practice, evaluation, and participatory quality assurance processes. The activity is designed for youth workers, organisation leaders, NGO managers, board members, and representatives of National Agencies and umbrella bodies who support quality development in the youth sector. items.description_text: MindBoost Academy is an international Erasmus+ training course that brings together youth workers, youth leaders, educators, trainers, volunteers, and other professionals from the Netherlands and Serbia active in the field of non-formal learning and youth work. Across Europe, youth workers increasingly encounter young people experiencing stress, anxiety, loneliness, burnout, and other mental health challenges. While youth workers are often a trusted source of support, many feel they lack practical tools and confidence to respond effectively. MindBoost Academy has been designed to strengthen their competences through experiential learning, international cooperation, and the exchange of good practices. A central outcome of the training is the co-creation of the MindBoost Toolkit—a practical collection of methods, activities, facilitation guides, and resources that participants will design together throughout the week. Rather than simply testing existing materials, participants will actively contribute their own experiences, ideas, and expertise to develop tools that can be adapted and implemented in youth work settings across different communities. During six days in Breda, participants will: - strengthen their understanding of youth mental health and wellbeing; - explore practical, non-formal education methods for promoting resilience and emotional wellbeing; - develop facilitation, mentoring, and peer-support skills; - learn how to recognise challenges and respond appropriately within the role of a youth worker; - co-create the MindBoost Toolkit, ensuring it reflects diverse experiences and practical needs from both partner countries; - build lasting connections with fellow youth workers and organisations. The programme is based on non-formal education, combining interactive workshops, simulations, reflection, peer learning, teamwork, creativity, and intercultural exchange. items.description_text: This course explores how youth work can become genuinely inclusive — moving beyond a declarative discourse on diversity towards everyday practice. Starting from the participants' own experience, we examine the common pitfalls that organisations, programmes and facilitators fall into (tokenism, surface-level or performative inclusion, assuming a space is neutral, one-size-fits-all approaches, accessibility treated as an afterthought, unconscious bias in recruitment and facilitation) and we build concrete solutions for designing learning and growth environments that value diversity. Participants work hands-on with one or two inclusion audit tools that they can apply afterwards in their own organisations and programmes. The methodology is non-formal and experiential, based on reflection, case studies and transfer to each participant's own context. items.description_text: PhEU – Philosophize EU (21st - 30th October, travel days included) is an Erasmus+ training course for youthworkers who want to explore what Europe means today and how philosophical dialogue can support critical thinking, democratic participation and active citizenship among young people. The project aims to: explore Europe as a philosophical, historical and ethical project; strengthen youth workers’ understanding of European values, human rights and citizenship; develop skills to facilitate dialogue on complex and sensitive topics; learn how to manage conflicting opinions and polarization constructively; provide practical methods to foster critical thinking and participation among young people. The training will be based on non-formal education, experiential learning and philosophical practice. Participants will take part in: team-building and reflection on personal and European values; philosophical dialogue and different debate methodologies; systemic consensing and Nonviolent Communication; simulations, role-playing and LARP-inspired activities; activities on European history, values, human rights and citizenship; activities connected to the Youth Work Agenda. Throughout the course, participants will reflect on how these methods can be adapted and used in their own youth-work contexts. The final part of the training will focus on transferring the learning into practice. Participants will work together to create an open educational toolkit with practical, ready-to-use activities that can later be adapted and tested with young people in their local communities.

items.description_text: This training is part of the “Engage, Connect and Empower Local Youth Councils in Europe” (ECE-LYCE) project. It addresses the mismatch identified between current LYC outreach efforts and their broader local demographics. Recognising that a significant majority of councils struggle with public relations and require advanced skills in digital branding and storytelling, this course instructs participants on how to move past dry, bureaucratic announcements toward dynamic, narrative-driven digital communication. The curriculum focuses on inclusive outreach strategies to break the inner "activism bubble" and intentionally engage historically underrepresented, marginalised, or non-active youth populations. To ensure these diversification efforts result in long-term retention rather than immediate dropout, the training combines external promotion with internal support systems. Participants will learn about structured onboarding protocols, peer-to-peer "buddy systems," and membership rotation models to stop the fragile practice of informal knowledge loss when senior members leave the LYC. With these integrated communication and mentoring frameworks LYCs will be equipped to broaden their visibility to the wider population and build sustainable channels for diverse civic participation. The methodology is based on non-formal education principles, combining peer learning, group work, simulations, case studies, reflection activities, and exchange of practices among participants from different local realities.

items.description_text: Are you a youth leader or youth worker committed to becoming an agent of change in your local community and beyond? Are you interested in learning more about what quality youth participation means and how you can embed it in your organisational life or the new projects that you plan? Do you want to explore the opportunities of the Erasmus+ Programme? Then “Dive into Youth Participation” is the Training Course for you! Youth participation in democratic life and young people's active civic engagement are high priorities of the EU Youth Strategy and are incorporated into the majority of contemporary youth policy frameworks in different European countries. The Erasmus+ Programme is one of the mechanisms to put the EU Youth Strategy into practice and provide many opportunities for young people to develop international projects, which empower them to take an active role in society and help them develop civic and social competencies. In this context, the fourth edition of the Training Course “Dive into Youth Participation” brings together 25 youth leaders and youth workers from different European countries with an aim to improve their understanding and practices toward quality youth participation. This is also an opportunity to learn more about the possibilities within the Erasmus+ Key Action 154 “Youth Participation Activities” and how to ensure youth participation is properly implemented in all stages of a project or participation initiative. Profile of participants The call is open for youth leaders and youth workers who fit the following criteria: -representatives of youth/youth work organisations or informal groups of young people; -have experience with youth participation or civic engagement; -are interested in developing projects within the Erasmus+ Key Action 154 “Youth Participation Activities” (no prior experience is required); -are interested in developing/improving youth participation practices/projects at any level (local, national, European or international)

Not every young person finds it easy to explain what they feel, where they belong or what they have experienced. Sometimes conversation alone is not enough. A photograph, fictional character, movement, memory, voice recording or a few written lines can open a different door. During the training, participants will experiment with: • creative autobiography and personal storytelling • creative writing • autobiographical theatre and movement • Photovoice and visual storytelling • Digital Storytelling • identity, voice and self-expression • emotional literacy and reflective practice • consent, boundaries and ethical storytelling • trauma-aware and inclusive facilitation • peer learning and intercultural exchange • adapting creative methods to everyday youth work The training is based on non-formal education and learning by doing. Participants will write, photograph, move, create, experiment, work in groups, reflect and exchange practice. This is not a lecture-based training. Because personal stories can involve sensitive material, particular attention will be given to consent, boundaries, emotional safety and ethical facilitation. items.title: Common Ground: Linking Ecology and Peacebuilding
items.summary: We aim to equip 32 youth workers with tools to connect ecology and peacebuilding, addressing climate change, conflict and social cohesion while strengthening peaceful, sustainable communities.

items.description_text: More info about the training: https://youthpeaceambassadors.medium.com/call-for-participants-common-ground-linking-ecology-and-peacebuilding-5743ecf030ed?sharedUserId=youthpeaceambassadors Common Ground brings together people who want to explore the connection between ecology and peacebuilding. Together, we will look at how environmental issues can contribute to conflict, but also how nature, cooperation, and shared resources can become powerful spaces for dialogue, connection, and peace. Through non-formal education, experiential learning, creative methods, and time in nature, we will explore practical tools that youth workers can use to engage young people with environmental peacebuilding, conflict transformation, and collective action. What you will take away from this: To build participants understanding of the interlinkages between ecology, climate change, and peacebuilding, exploring how environmental issues fuel conflict and how peacebuilding approaches can promote ecological justice. To equip participants with practical tools and methods for eco-peacebuilding, including conflict transformation in environmental disputes, eco-anxiety support, and community resilience practices. To strengthen participant’s competences in facilitating dialogue and cooperation across divides (generational, cultural, political) in the context of ecological challenges and sustainability transitions. To foster creative and community-based approaches for promoting a culture of peace through ecological action, such as storytelling, artivism, conflict transformation, and participatory futures thinking. To support participants in designing at least 5 local eco-peacebuilding initiatives in their communities. To strengthen international cooperation among youth workers, building networks, exchanging good practices, and fostering collaboration for future European eco-peacebuilding initiatives.

items.description_text: Growing Together project connects youth workers motivated to support learning, participation and inclusion of young parents in their communities. The aim is to provide youth workers an opportunity to develop their competencies and toolkit needed to work with young parents - people who have had a baby before the age of 25. The project rises the question why young parents are often not seen as a target group of youth work and why there are so few activities that are tailored for their needs - at European level in international mobilities but also in local activities and youth spaces which often do not explicitly welcome young parents. We hope to make youth work more inclusive towards young parents and create more participation and learning opportunities to young parents in our communities and countries. We welcome youth workers, facilitators, trainers and mentors, motivated to empower young parents, especially to foster their active participation in their communities and to contribute to creating more supportive and more inclusive environments. During the training course, 26 youth workers will share methods and tools that they already use in their work with young parents, as well as develop and test new methods. A special focus will be put on learning methods that allow parents participate in activities together with their children providing learning benefits for both, children and adults. We will explore how expressive arts, storytelling and creative expression can help young people talk about risky behaviour, unhealthy relationships, digital risks and gender stereotypes. The programme mixes hands-on creative workshops, inputs from experts, peer learning and time to plan future projects together. There will be some lectures, but most of the time you will be active, trying things out and working with others. We also focus on equal opportunities in artistic communities, such as dancers, actors and circus performers, who often face pressure around body image and gender roles. items.description_text: About the project Many young people spend increasing amounts of time indoors and online, while nature can be a vital source of connection, well-being and resilience. This training helps youth workers experience nature as an active part of the learning process, not just a backdrop. Participants slow down, observe, and explore their own relationship with nature — then critically reflect on what place nature holds in their youth work now, and could hold in the future. Aim & objectives The training supports youth workers in integrating nature-based learning and eco-friendly practices into their everyday work, strengthening competences in facilitation, activity design, reflection, and translating insights into practice. It follows five steps: Connect (building a safe foundation with self, others and nature), Experience (exploring nature-based methods for well-being and resilience), Critically explore (examining personal nature values and their role in practice), Design (creating activities using a practical template), and Take action (developing a concrete plan for their own work and organisation). Learning approach The training is based on Nature-Based Learning (NBL): learning in, from and about nature, spending as much time outdoors as possible. Through experiential learning — slowing down, observing, and harvesting insights — participants connect experience to practice and move toward concrete action. Central to the approach is a reciprocal relationship with nature: learning from it while exploring how this connection inspires care and responsibility.

Throughout the week, participants will explore practical tools and techniques to use drawings, symbols, visual structures and creative methods to communicate ideas and information in a clearer and more engaging way. The main goal is not to become a professional artist. It is to discover how visual thinking can improve the way we facilitate groups, share information and create educational experiences. The training will give participants the opportunity to practice these methods and develop the confidence to incorporate them into their own educational and youth work activities. WHAT WILL YOU GET FROM THE TRAINING? You will have the chance to: • Learn more about graphic facilitation and visual methods • Develop practical skills for presenting ideas visually • Discover new ways to make educational activities clearer, more creative and engaging • Practice graphic facilitation and graphic recording • Build confidence in using visual tools in your own activities • Exchange methods and experiences with people working with young people across Europe • Create new international connections and opportunities for cooperation TWO EXPERIENCED FACILITATORS The training will be delivered by Helena Podlešákova Leszczyńska and Urszula Leszczyńska, two experienced trainers and graphic facilitators from the NGO sector. Together, they have co-founded YoWo Poland, bringing experience from international youth work, Erasmus+ projects and visual facilitation to the training. INTERESTED? At the same time, many youth workers are interested in addressing these topics but do not always have practical methodologies, structured frameworks or sufficient confidence to transform sustainability concepts into engaging non-formal education activities. The Green Future project responds to this need by introducing participants to GreenComp - the European Sustainability Competence Framework and exploring how it can be practically applied in youth work. The training course will gather youth workers from Austria, Croatia, Germany, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Montenegro and create an international learning environment where participants can exchange experiences, explore different local realities and jointly develop approaches for sustainability education. items.description_text: The Edge Within is an Erasmus+ Training Course for youth workers, trainers, facilitators, educators, community leaders and others actively involved — professionally or voluntarily — in youth work and non-formal learning. Many of us support young people in navigating change, uncertainty, relationships and questions of identity — while meeting similar edges within ourselves. The Edge Within is an invitation to turn some of that attention inward. For one week, 25 participants from Czechia, Latvia, Romania, Italy and Estonia will step away from their everyday routines and gather at an old Scout base surrounded by forests in Nejdek, Czech Republic. Together, we will explore the “edges” within ourselves: our patterns, reactions, boundaries, strengths and the places where we meet uncertainty, discomfort or the not-yet-known. And we will ask how greater awareness of these processes can influence the way we listen, facilitate, hold space and accompany young people. The training combines personal exploration with professional reflection. Through experiential and non-formal learning, nature-based and embodied practices, storytelling, creative expression, movement, reflection, peer learning and community living, participants will first experience the methods themselves — and then explore how they can be meaningfully and ethically adapted to their own youth work. We are looking for people who are curious, open to reflection and willing to participate fully in an experiential learning process. You do not need to be an experienced trainer or have previous experience with nature-based approaches. The setting itself will be part of the journey. We will live simply and closely together, spend meaningful time outdoors and experience November in the Czech countryside as it comes. In a world marked by growing complexity, the need for conflict transformation has never been more urgent. This project invites participants to take a step back, return to the fundamentals, and rediscover the power of dialogue and understanding. Are you ready to shape a new narrative? items.description_text: Wellness Navigators Webinar Series Wellness Navigators is a series of six free online webinars created for youth workers, educators, trainers, facilitators, and anyone interested in supporting the emotional and social well-being of young people. Running from September 2026 to February 2027, the series explores practical approaches to well-being through the four dimensions of the Wellness Compass: Body, Mind, Emotions, and Connection. Each webinar combines accessible theory with practical tools, reflection, and experiential activities that can be used both for personal development and in educational work with young people. Topics include emotional awareness and regulation, connection and empathy, body-based practices, play and joy, and everyday strategies for strengthening resilience and well-being. The webinars are part of the Wellness Navigators Erasmus+ project, which develops practical educational resources to help young people better recognise their needs, understand their emotional and bodily signals, build healthier relationships, and navigate everyday challenges with greater awareness and choice. What to expect Participants will: discover practical tools for supporting youth well-being; explore the connection between body, thoughts, emotions, and relationships; learn experiential activities that can be adapted to youth work and non-formal education; gain inspiration from approaches such as Nonviolent Communication, embodiment, mindfulness, creative methods, and emotional education; receive access to webinar recordings and additional project resources. The webinars are free of charge and open to an international audience. Participants can register once for the whole six-part series and receive information and access links before each session. The webinar series accompanies the development of the Wellness Navigators toolkit and card deck, offering an opportunity to explore some of the ideas and practices behind the resources in greater depth. items.description_text: Humour is already present in youth work practice - but it's rarely used as a deliberate, structured tool. "Humour is Serious Business" (HiSB) is a 6-day Erasmus+ KA153-YOU training course (27 November - 3 December 2026, Hollókő, Hungary) that will help you turn something you probably already do instinctively into an intentional, ethical, and effective competence for engaging young people. This training is aimed specifically at practitioners in the field of non-formal learning and youth work - not at the general public. You should apply if you are a youth worker (professional or voluntary), a youth leader, a young person (18+) with leadership potential already identified by your organisation, or a practitioner with relevant expertise who works with young people (e.g. a coach, mentor or tutor), even if youth work is not your primary profession. Through non-formal methods - World Café, simulations and role play, clowning and improvisation, team building, and daily reflection groups - you will explore the many different types of humour, examine cultural differences in how humour is used, reflect on your own sense of humour, and develop concrete post-programme actions to bring back to your own community. Every participant leaves with a Personal Development Plan and the chance to earn a Youthpass. HiSB is delivered by an experienced international Training Team and hosted by MAVISZ (Hungary), together with partner organisations in Poland, Portugal, Armenia, Serbia, Latvia, Croatia, Montenegro and Spain. 36 participants will take part, 4 per sending country. Participants will begin with curiosity-based challenges and exploratory activities, investigating conductivity and discovering how everyday objects, water, fruit, aluminium foil, graphite, recycled materials and other conductive surfaces can become computer inputs. They will then explore how Makey Makey can be connected with Scratch and used to create interactive digital experiences such as sound installations, interactive posters, musical instruments, collaborative games, storytelling activities, art projects and team-building challenges. The STEAM approach will be embedded throughout the training: Science through conductivity, circuits and experimentation. Technology through Makey Makey and Scratch. Engineering through designing and testing interactive systems. Arts through music, storytelling, visual expression and creative design. Mathematics through sequencing, patterns, logic and problem-solving. The training is based on non-formal education principles and prioritises learning by doing, collaboration, experimentation, peer learning, reflection and active participation. items.description_text: The European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC) invites youth workers, youth leaders, trainers, community practitioners and other professionals working in non-formal learning and youth work to join the first session of Equal Ground, a quarterly ENRMSC dialogue series exploring meaningful participation, access to opportunities and accountability. About the session A seat at the table means little if the decisions are already made. Equal Ground Q1: Meaningful Participation — Beyond the Seat at the Table explores what meaningful participation looks like when refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities are not simply invited into conversations, but have genuine opportunities to influence decisions, policies and actions. The session will examine the difference between being present and participating meaningfully. Who gets invited to the table? Who gets heard? Who gets to influence what happens next? Through a participatory, community-centred dialogue, participants will explore barriers to meaningful participation and consider how youth workers, organisations and institutions can create more effective pathways for people with lived experience to contribute to decision-making. What will participants explore? The session will explore: • Meaningful participation beyond consultation and representation • The difference between having a seat at the table and having influence • How lived experience can contribute to knowledge, leadership and decision-making • Barriers that can prevent refugees, migrants, stateless people and other communities from participating meaningfully • The role of youth workers and non-formal learning practitioners in creating inclusive participation • How organisations can listen to communities and translate their perspectives into action • How young people and community changemakers can move from participation to leadership • Practical approaches for creating more inclusive spaces for dialogue and decision-mak

items.description_text: Life in It is a two-part Erasmus+ media training for people active in youth work and non-formal learning, including youth workers, trainers, educators, volunteers, project coordinators and people involved in their organisation’s communication. No previous filmmaking experience is required; the focus is on learning through practice, collaboration and experimentation. The learning journey starts with online preparation and continues with Frame One in Germany (13–19 December 2026), where participants explore practical filmmaking, storytelling and media tools by working in international crews and creating content in real local contexts. Between the two international phases, participants bring the learning into their own organisation or community, including a small focus group with young people and further local practice. The journey continues with Frame Two at Hopeland, Greece (22–29 September 2027), where participants explore how the same storytelling foundations can be adapted to shorter, vertical video and social media formats. The methodology is strongly based on non-formal education and learning by doing: short inputs, practical assignments, teamwork, feedback, reflection and creative decision-making are at the centre of the programme. Life in It is designed as one learning journey rather than two separate trainings, with online preparation, two residential phases, local practice and follow-up. Priority is given to applicants who can take part in the complete process and use the learning afterwards in their youth work, organisation or local community.

A core aim is to promote civic engagement through digital tools. Objectives: Strengthen Digital Competencies: Provide practical training in ICT, social media engagement, and digital content creation. items.description_text: The ENRMSC European Dialogue & Capacity-Building Forum 2027 will take place in Warsaw, Poland, in April 2027. The forum will bring together young refugees, migrants and stateless changemakers, youth workers, youth leaders, researchers, academics, civil society organisations, public institutions and other practitioners working with young people. The forum is built around a simple question: How can we move from young people being affected by systems to young people meaningfully shaping knowledge, opportunities, policies and solutions? The programme will explore meaningful participation, access to education and professional opportunities, community leadership, research and evidence, youth engagement, advocacy and collaboration between communities and institutions. Participants will take part in interactive discussions, panel sessions, workshops and facilitated group activities. The programme will combine knowledge exchange with practical capacity-building and opportunities for participants to develop new connections and potential European cooperation. A particular focus will be placed on recognising lived experience as expertise. Young refugees, migrants and stateless people will not only participate as beneficiaries but as contributors, knowledge holders, community leaders and partners in shaping discussions and recommendations. The forum will also connect participants with relevant European opportunities, networks and potential partners, including opportunities related to youth work, education, research, leadership and civic participation. The event is particularly relevant to people working in non-formal learning and youth work who engage with young people from refugee, migrant and stateless backgrounds. The guiding principle of the forum is: “Nothing About Us Without Us.” The forum is currently being developed by the European Network of Refugee, Migrant and Stateless Changemakers (ENRMSC), a refugee-, migrant- and stateless-led European civil society organisation.

items.description_text: Why this programme? Young people increasingly experience the world through digital, visual, interactive and participatory media. At the same time, heritage education can sometimes remain centred on traditional formats: guided tours, exhibitions, historical information and passive observation. This creates an opportunity for youth work. New media can provide alternative entry points into heritage, allowing young people to: explore places and stories through immersive experiences; discover hidden or forgotten narratives; connect personal and community memories with wider European heritage; question dominant interpretations of history; create their own narratives; collaborate across cultures; transform physical spaces into interactive learning environments. The programme therefore does not aim to turn youth trainers into technology specialists. Instead, it aims to help them become creative facilitators who know when, why and how to use technology to create meaningful learning experiences. General aim To strengthen the capacity of youth trainers to use new media and emerging technologies as tools for heritage awareness, intercultural learning, creativity and youth participation.
